findings.paper_title: Item 15 Appointment of Independent Members (Audit and Governance Committee)

findings.detail: The report says the appointments are intended to meet the CIPFA best practice of at least two co-opted independent members for technical expertise. The Constitution allows up to three Independent Members, so the proposed three would fill that maximum.

findings.detail: The paper reports 16,958 claimants, 57% of whom are working age and 43% pensionable age. The count is 128 lower than at the same point last year.
findings.matters: Caseload direction is the main driver of scheme cost, so a fall in claimants matters for both budget forecasts and the council tax base.
findings.figures: 128 fewer claimants year on year; around 16,958 claimants; 57% working age; 43% pensionable age

findings.matters: Other councils setting or reviewing a minimum contribution can use this per-percentage-point cost to size the same trade-off.
findings.figures: c£133k per 1% movement in minimum payment; c£665k for a 20% scheme; 25% current minimum contribution

findings.detail: The paper says 2025/26 actual cost equalled the estimate assumed in the council tax base. It gives 2026/27 expenditure as £19.5m, and says this may change depending on caseload by year end.
findings.matters: The rise in scheme cost, and the council's view that it is still on budget, shows how a council funds a relief scheme that is paid for through the council tax base.

findings.matters: A finance director or lender tracking in-year collection will see that this council is running below its own target and the prior year at the half-year point.

The paper attributes the increase to ongoing housing growth together with the continued impact of Council Tax premiums and changes in the property tax base.
findings.matters: The tax base sets the Council Tax yield that councils and precepting authorities plan against, so a 1.4% rise in the base is a direct change to the income they can expect.

findings.matters: Independent validation of a transport forecasting method is relevant to any finance team facing the same mismatch between academic-year service and financial-year budgets.

findings.matters: A savings estimate that depends on capital investment and a consultation is one a finance director would want to see costed and tested before it enters the budget.
findings.figures: estimated savings over £350,000 per annum; several hundred mainstream pupils
findings.quote: delivering estimated savings of over £350,000 per annum.

findings.detail: Phase 1 was completed in Spring 2026 and identified five priority opportunities. The report says Phase 2 is now under way, delivered by council officers across the service, transformation, Adult Social Care, Children's Services and financial services.
findings.matters: Board approval of a business case with stated savings is the step at which a transformation project becomes a funded commitment that can be tracked.

findings.quote: was approved by the councils internal Transformation Board on the 26th October 2026.

findings.headline: Travel to School is expected to deliver £1.5m of savings over 2027/28 and 2028/29 under the T20 Transformation Programme.
findings.detail: The savings are attributed to Projects 7a and 7b of the T20 programme. The report sets out the workstreams that make up Phase 2, including Personal Travel Budgets, Independent Travel Training and a review of operator quality.
findings.matters: A stated £1.5m savings target over two years gives a finance director a figure to test against delivery in later monitoring reports.

findings.paper_title: Travel to School Overview, Demands and Transformation Activities
findings.headline: The Council names growing EHCP numbers as its largest risk on Travel to School finances.
findings.detail: The report identifies the growing number of EHCPs as the largest risk, noting its effect on council finances and a year-on-year rise in spend. It also lists school place sufficiency, inflation, fuel costs and operator supply as risks.
findings.matters: A council naming EHCP growth as its largest transport risk sets out the exposure that other councils with rising SEND caseloads will also carry.
findings.quote: The largest risk is the impact of the growing increase in EHCP’s and how this is having a significant effect on the finances of the council.

findings.paper_title: Travel to School Overview, Demands and Transformation Activities
findings.headline: Pupils receiving Travel to School support total 6115 in September 2026, an increase of circa 67% since August 2023.
findings.detail: The report breaks the 6115 pupils into 4191 mainstream, 1417 SEND, 238 post-16 mainstream and 269 post-16 SEND. It says the largest part of the increase is SEND pupils travelling to named schools.
findings.matters: A three-year rise of about two-thirds in transported pupils is a demand shift that other councils' transport budgets are likely to face in similar form.
findings.figures: 6115 pupils; 4191 mainstream; 1417 SEND; 238 post-16 mainstream; 269 post-16 SEND; circa 67% increase from August 2023
findings.quote: This is an increase of circa 67% from August 2023.

findings.headline: The EHCP cohort reached 6,032 in September 2026, 16.3% higher than twelve months earlier, the report says.
findings.detail: The report describes the EHCP cohort as at an all-time high. It states that around 30% of children with EHCPs receive transport support, and that this proportion is expected to rise.
findings.matters: Transport demand is tied to EHCP numbers, so a 16.3% year-on-year rise in the cohort feeds directly into council transport cost growth elsewhere.

findings.quote: The EHC cohort rose to an all time high of 6,032 in September 2026. The cohort is now 16.3% higher than 12 months ago.

findings.paper_title: Travel to School Overview, Demands and Transformation Activities

findings.quote: The 2026/27 budget is £26.7m, with a proposed increase to £31.8m in 2027/28, representing an increase of £5.1m.

The report says the financial year spans two academic years, so costs remain subject to change from new applications.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council running a demand-led transport budget will recognise the same pattern of spend being set on committed arrangements and then moving as new applications arrive.

findings.quote: Current modelling indicates a potential net financial benefit of £99,246 in 2027/28

findings.matters: The grant is the funding route that other councils in build-back will also rely on, so the amount is useful for comparison.

findings.matters: Finance team capacity and LGR legacy work are common pressures across councils, and this paper ties both directly to a backstopped audit.

The paper's principal factors are four years of disclaimed opinions and the council's finance team capacity.

Its key recommendation is to accelerate the transformation programme and to focus on the cost pressures in Children's Services.
findings.matters: A finance director at a peer council will compare its own medium-term gap and savings delivery against this, and a lender will see that the auditor has flagged the plan as insufficient.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - NNC Disclaimer of opinion 25-26

findings.detail: The auditor states it does not express an opinion on the accounts, because the matters in the basis for disclaimer section could be both material and pervasive. findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, will want to know how the disclaimer was reached and whether the backstop regime is pushing other authorities toward the same position.
findings.figures: Backstop date 31 January 2027; disclaimer on the year ended 31 March 2025 issued 24 February 2026
findings.quote: We do not express an opinion on the accompanying financial statements of the Authority.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B Letter of Representation 2025-26
findings.headline: Management did not adjust the 2025/26 financial statements for misstatements identified by the auditor, which it describes as immaterial

findings.matters: Unadjusted misstatements that management judges immaterial are a common point of challenge in audit committees, and peers may compare how their own materiality judgements are recorded.
findings.quote: We have not adjusted the financial statements for these misstatements brought to our attention as they are immaterial

findings.paper_title: Appendix B Letter of Representation 2025-26

findings.matters: Reclassifying investment properties changes how a council's asset base is presented, and a finance director or lender comparing years would need to know whether earlier figures were restated.
findings.quote: We have not undertaken a prior period adjustment in respect of the reclassification of investments properties

It notes that the Code requires auditors who cannot conclude their work to issue a qualified or disclaimed opinion by the backstop date.
findings.matters: A council that cannot supply balances for its largest asset classes by the backstop date risks a qualified or disclaimed audit opinion, which a lender and peer finance teams will track against their own deadlines.
findings.figures: Publication date for 2025/26 financial statements: 31 January 2027

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26

findings.detail: Six recommendations from the 2024/25 audit were followed up. The auditor reports completed actions for IFRS 16, PPE classification, accrued income supporting evidence, and audit trails and responses to audit queries, with suitable audit trails now provided and queries answered within agreed timescales. Cash and cash equivalents were also reported with no issues identified.
findings.matters: A documented closure of prior-year audit recommendations shows the progress a council can make in a single year after a disclaimer.

findings.quote: We have been provided with suitable audit trails to support entries within the financial statements.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Auditor expects to deliver an unqualified opinion for the 2029/30 financial statements, with the assurance rebuilding strategy presented to committee in August 2026
findings.detail: The auditor states that it has made substantial progress compared with the prior year audit, and that the financial statements presented for audit were a significant improvement and the working papers of higher quality. It also says it remains on plan to move to an unqualified opinion for 2029/30, using the Regaining Assurance Strategy presented to the committee on 17 August 2026.
findings.matters: A stated date for returning to an unqualified opinion, with progress described as substantial, is a recovery timetable that finance directors and lenders can track.

findings.quote: We remain on plan to move to an unqualified opinion for the 2029/30 financial statements.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Investment property review transfers £113.262m to land and buildings, with the auditor saying the change is a prior year classification error and officers declining a prior period adjustment
findings.detail: Officers reviewed the investment property portfolio and transferred £113.262m from investment properties to land and buildings. The auditor found no issues with the transfer but concluded that, because there was no change in use, it corrects a prior year classification error requiring a prior period adjustment. Officers declined to make that adjustment. Testing of revalued investment properties also led to a £4.456m increase after four valuation inputs were corrected.
findings.matters: Reclassifying investment property at this scale, with the auditor and officers disagreeing on the correct treatment, is an issue for other councils that hold investment property portfolios.
findings.figures: £113.262m transfer; £4.456m revaluation increase; 4 assets
findings.quote: As there has been no change in the use for these assets this adjustment represents a prior year classification error, which would require correction through a prior period adjustment rather than a current year transfer. Officers have declined to undertake a prior period adjustment.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Auditor identifies a difference of £6.134m in creditor balances and £2.451m in debtor balances with West Northamptonshire Council, which would reduce reserves by c£3.5m
findings.detail: The auditor compared the council's inter-council balances with West Northamptonshire Council and found differences of £6.134m for creditors and £2.451m for debtors, which indicates the balances were not agreed before the statements were prepared. If adjusted, these would reduce the council's reserves by about £3.5m. The council is working with West Northamptonshire Council to resolve the positions.
findings.matters: A reserves reduction of about £3.5m from inter-council differences shows how unagreed balances between councils can affect a reserve position.
findings.figures: £6.134m creditor difference; £2.451m debtor difference; c£3.5m reserves impact
findings.quote: We note that if these amounts are adjusted for that they would reduce the Authority's reserves by c£3.5m.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Unadjusted misstatements total £7.276m on a cumulative basis, including £3.78m for the current year and £4.902m extrapolated from the prior year
findings.detail: The auditor identified current year unadjusted misstatements of £3.78m, which management has not adjusted because the amount is not material and figures are still being verified with West Northamptonshire Council. Prior year extrapolated errors on short-term debtors of £4.902m are carried forward, giving a cumulative impact of £7.276m on the 2025/26 statements.
findings.matters: Uncorrected misstatements that the committee is asked to approve are a disclosed risk to reported reserves, relevant to any council carrying similar balances.
findings.figures: £3.78m current year; £4.902m prior year extrapolated; £7.276m cumulative
findings.quote: Cumulative impact of prior year and current year unadjusted misstatements on 2025/26 financial statements 7,276 (7,276) 7,276 7,276

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Prior period adjustments removed 7 academy schools (NBV £40.167m) from the asset register after they should have been disposed of in earlier years
findings.detail: Testing of property, plant and equipment disposals found 7 schools with a net book value of £40.167m that should have been removed when they became academies in previous years. Officers have applied a prior period adjustment to recognise the disposals in the correct year.
findings.matters: Academy conversions leaving schools on a council's asset register are a common issue across councils, and a prior period adjustment of this size affects comparative figures.
findings.figures: 7 schools; NBV £40.167m
findings.quote: Our testing of Property. Plant and Equipment disposals (£68.785m) identified that it included 7 schools (NBV £40.167m) that should have been disposed of in previous years when the schools became an Academy.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Adjusted misstatements reduce the council's 2025/26 comprehensive income and expenditure by £43.321m across four adjustments
findings.detail: The auditor identified four adjustments to the financial statements, which together produced a £43.321m adjustment to the Comprehensive Income and Expenditure Statement. The adjustments include the Children's Trust consolidation, disposal of Academy schools, disposal of fully depreciated assets, and the investment property revaluation.
findings.matters: A £43.321m adjustment to reported income and expenditure is large relative to the materiality threshold and shows the scale of corrections needed to reach a set of accounts.
findings.figures: £43.321m adjustment to CIES; four adjustments
findings.quote: We have identified four adjustments to the financial statements, resulting in a £43.321m adjustment to the Authority's Comprehensive Income and Expenditure Statement.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Northamptonshire Children's Trust not consolidated in 2025/26 draft accounts or prior years, with a prior period adjustment made and the 2025/26 consolidation left unconcluded
findings.detail: The draft statements presented for audit did not include the council's share of the Trust's accounts, and the Trust had not been consolidated for previous years. The council has made a prior period adjustment and adjusted for the 2025/26 omission, but the auditor could not complete work on the consolidation because the Trust's own audit is incomplete. The backstop date for 2026/27 is brought forward to 30 November 2027 from 31 January 2027 for 2025/26.
findings.matters: A council's share of a children's trust may be a material consolidation exposure, and a backstop date moving earlier affects every council with a similar arm's-length vehicle.
findings.figures: backstop 31 January 2027 (2025/26); 30 November 2027 (2026/27 as stated in the action plan)
findings.quote: For 2026/27 the backstop date is being brought forward to 30 November (from 31 January 2027 for 2025/26).

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Street Lighting PFI model may understate closing liability by £5.386m, with officers agreeing to review the model for 2026/27
findings.detail: Following IFRS 16 implementation, the auditor identified differences in how indexation of the fair value of operating expenses was calculated. This could mean a potential understatement of £5.386m of the closing liability. The model is to be reviewed for 2026/27.
findings.matters: PFI model errors arising from IFRS 16 implementation are a risk other councils with similar schemes may need to check.
findings.figures: £5.386m potential understatement
findings.quote: This has resulted in a potential understatement of £5.386m of the closing liability.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Shaw Elderly Persons Homes contract reclassified from public private partnership to service contract, reducing PPE by £20.6m and creditors by £20.6m
findings.detail: After the auditor challenged the accounting treatment, management agreed the Shaw Elderly Persons Homes contract does not meet the definition of a PPP and should be treated as a service contract. This reduced PPE by £20.6m and reduced short-term and long-term creditors by £1.8m and £18.78m, and reduced net operating expenditure by £1.216m. It also led to a prior period adjustment.
findings.matters: Reclassifying a PFI-style contract changes both the asset and liability balances on the balance sheet, which is relevant to other councils with similar arrangements.
findings.figures: PPE reduced £20.6m; short-term creditors £1.8m; long-term creditors £18.78m; net operating expenditure reduced £1.216m
findings.quote: Management have reviewed the accounting treatment and confirmed that the contract does not meet the definition of a PPP and should be treated as a service contract

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Unidentified inherited debtors and creditors from predecessor bodies stand at £35.146m and £28.805m, with the council's share potentially around 50%
findings.detail: West Northamptonshire Council is leading a project to address unidentified debtors and creditors inherited from predecessor councils, which is expected to take around two years. findings.quote: At November 2026 officers believe these figures are £35.146m of unidentified debtors and £28.805m of unidentified creditors (net position £6.341m).

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Land and buildings valuation testing finds floor plans not provided for 21 assets (£85.98m) and rent evidence not provided for 5 assets (£11.3m)
findings.detail: Testing of the 2025/26 revaluations identified 21 assets (£85.98m) with no floor plans to support gross internal areas, 5 assets (£11.3m) with no rent passing evidence, and one formula error that valued an asset at nil instead of £1.12m. The auditor says it has not been able to gain assurance over the 2025/26 valuations of land and buildings and surplus assets and will include this in its report.
findings.matters: Indexation of PPE in intervening years is new from 2025/26 under the Code, so valuation evidence gaps affect any council adopting the same approach.

findings.quote: For 21 assets (£85.98m) officers were unable to provide floor plans to support the gross internal areas used in the valuations.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Auditor's materiality set at £16.3m, with the 2024/25 materiality reconsidered at year-end following a rise in gross expenditure
findings.detail: The planning materiality of £16.3m, based on 1.9% of prior year gross expenditure, was reconsidered at year end using draft financial statements. Performance materiality is £8.965m, and misstatements above £0.815m are reported.
findings.matters: The materiality threshold sets the scale of errors the auditor treats as significant, which is a useful benchmark for finance teams in comparable authorities.
findings.figures: £16.3m materiality; £8.965m performance materiality; £0.815m reporting threshold
findings.quote: We have determined materiality at £16.3m based on professional judgement

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Audit Findings (ISA260) Report - 25-26
findings.headline: Auditor notes the council is considering applying for Exceptional Financial Support for its 2027/28 budget, while officers say reserves would cover a 2027/28 deficit if support is not provided
findings.detail: The auditor records the council is considering EFS for 2027/28 and comments on it in the Auditor's Annual Report. Officers have indicated that without EFS the council would still have sufficient reserves to meet any 2027/28 deficit.

findings.headline: Auditor identifies two significant weaknesses in value for money arrangements and is not satisfied the council has made proper arrangements for economy, efficiency and effectiveness

findings.headline: Auditor expects to issue a disclaimed opinion on the 2025/26 financial statements, with the audit not completed before the 31 January 2027 backstop date
findings.detail: The auditor states it has been unable to undertake sufficient work to support an unmodified opinion before the backstop date, and that the limitations on opening balances mean it will be unable to form an opinion on the financial statements. The prior year's audit was also disclaimed.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion on a second consecutive year means that councils using this authority's accounts as a benchmark, and lenders assessing its financial reporting, have no audited assurance over opening balances.
findings.figures: Backstop date 31 January 2027

findings.matters: Repeated IT general controls findings bear on how the external auditor approaches the financial statements audit, and a finance director elsewhere would want to know how such repeats are handled.

findings.matters: A lender needs to understand the council's maximum risk tolerance for school deficits; a peer council can benchmark its own thresholds.

findings.matters: A lender assessing the council's exposure needs to understand it has accepted a permanent liability for school deficits that only schools themselves can resolve.
